params.source: Selection tab. 'No treatment' = average CER vs untreated baseline. 'Current treatment' = incremental ICER vs the standard-of-care drug for each use category (Src-Comparators).

params.label: FX rate applied to money (LCU per USD)
params.source: Src-CE Thresholds FX table (fx_countries / fx_rates). THE currency switch: 1 when USD is selected, else the country rate. Applied exactly ONCE per cost family at its effective column — medication (Src-Med Costs AN), HRH (Src-HRH Unit Costs L), inpatient (Control D47), side-effects (Calc-SE E), thresholds (D24, numeric branches only), BIA money pulls (Calc-BIA C23/C24). Never applied to DALYs, percentages, adherence or admin %. QC A26 proves no consumer is missed or double-counted.

params.label: Real-world effectiveness multiplier
params.source: Set to 1.0 (2026-08-20): the previous 0.8 had no source (Singla 2017 is psychological-therapy literature) and double-counted adherence, the main efficacy-effectiveness mechanism for medications (WHO-CHOICE applies a single ×⅔ adjustment). 0.8 retained as a one-way sensitivity scenario.

params.label: Default oral medication adherence
params.source: Ascher-Svanum 2008 (58% overall, MPR>80%); Lacro 2002 (50–59%); WHO/Sabaté 2003 (~50% long-term therapies). 0.60 = upper-middle of the band.

params.label: Default LAI adherence
params.source: Einarson 2012, Ann Gen Psychiatry 11:18, Table 1 (observed LAI receipt 0.823–0.872); set at the upper end per owner decision 2026-08-20; tornado 0.75–0.95.

params.label: Default short-acting IM adherence

params.label: Cobenfy (KarXT) adherence

params.label: Product-mix basis for BIA budgets
params.source: Current tx (incumbent) = country product mix (Src-Demand MIX DEFAULTS). CE-optimised = dashboard cabinet winner at 100% per category. Global selector on Budget Impact; per-category override in each mix table.

params.label: Apply survival (mortality) benefit?
params.source: Aymerich 2024 meta-analysis (17 studies); Taipale 2020 World Psychiatry (FIN20 HR 0.48); Tiihonen 2009/2017 (FIN11 HR 0.81); Correll 2022 (treated-vs-untreated HR 0.71); clozapine HR 0.74 (register series). Observational GRADE — RCT meta (Kishimoto 2016) found no difference. Base case from vS (owner decision 2026-09-14): survival benefit included, all three layers (any antipsychotic vs none HR 0.71; extra LAI-vs-oral OR 0.79; extra clozapine HR 0.74). Trial-evidence-only view retained as the Sensitivity scenario row. Inputs: Src-Inpatient Costs mortality block (C42:C46). User switch: Setup → Advanced settings.

params.label: Medication costing basis
params.source: Owner decision 2026-09-10. 'Full course (incl. wastage)' = the CEA costs 100% of prescribed units — what procurement actually pays — and Calc-Direct col AH shows the unconsumed share as wastage. 'Consumed doses only' = the standard CEA convention (medication cost scaled by adherence). Single switch point: Calc-Direct col F. Effects are ALWAYS adherence-scaled in both states, so the E=P tier identity (QC A10) is unchanged. The BIA is NOT governed by this parameter — it keeps the demand-model wastage method (P_BIA_ADHERENCE row 104 + P_BIA_WASTAGE row 102). User input: Setup Advanced settings.

params.label: Apply treatment effect on admissions?
params.source: Owner decision 2026-09-11. Treated patients are admitted less often than untreated — class RR 0.43 (0.32–0.57), Ceraso 2020 Cochrane CD008016; product overrides for clozapine / olanzapine / quetiapine on Src-Inpatient Costs rows 49–53. Adherence scales the benefit (Calc-Direct col AJ: 1 − adherence × (1 − RR)). When ON, P_ADM_DIFF (row 48) is forced idle — the LAI admission credit is carried by adherence inside AJ. User input: Setup → Advanced settings.

params.label: Admission-rate basis
params.source: Owner decision 2026-09-11. Comparator-rebased (default): the country's admission % (P_INPT_SCZ_ACUTE) describes patients on the current Initiation+Maintenance treatment; untreated rate = admission % ÷ RR-effective of that comparator (Calc-Direct col AK). Untreated baseline (alternative, conservative): treats the country's admission % as the untreated rate. User input: Setup → Advanced settings.

params.label: Transfer-factor method
params.source: Owner decision 2026-09-11. Proportional (default): Q = k_prop × baseline DW (Src-Transition Factors row 18; 0.284 = 0.181/0.638, Andrews 2003 / Chisholm 2008 WHO-CHOICE equivalent 0.289). Absolute (Andrews literal): Q = the applied 0.181 (Src-Transition Factors col E) — reproduces the pre-change chain. User input: Setup → Advanced settings.

params.label: Cap health gain at the GBD acute–stable gap
params.source: Owner decision 2026-09-11. Caps monotherapy improvement at the GBD acute→residual gap (baseline DW − DW_residual 0.588; ET severe 0.190) — a treated patient is never modelled as better than GBD's stable residual state. Binds only for clozapine at defaults (0.197 → 0.190). Salomon 2015 Lancet Glob Health. User input: Setup → Advanced settings. vS 2026-09-14: Setup row hidden (wiring intact via Setup!D29); plain-language: never credits more improvement than the gap between acute and stable schizophrenia (0.19 DW units); affects clozapine only (−3%).

cabinetConfig.description: The most cost-effective medications to manage psychosis across the full treatment pathway, including treatment initation, maintenance, treatment-resistance, and acute agitation.
Recommended drugs to manage depression — first-line SSRIs, second-line TCAs, CBT adjunct therapy, and combined pharmacotherapy + psychotherapy for moderate-severe or treatment-resistant cases.
Recommended drugs for bipolar disorder maintenance — first-line mood stabilisers (lithium, valproate) and second-line alternatives (carbamazepine).
Recommended drugs to manage anxiety disorders — first-line SSRIs and CBT adjunct therapy for moderate-severe generalised anxiety.
